# temps_environment_workflow_settings (Resource)

Limits of the durable workflows an environment runs. Values left out keep their current setting. Destroying the resource leaves the settings as they are.

Import with `<project_id>/<environment_id>`.

Required API key permissions: `workflows:read`, `workflows:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "temps_environment_workflow_settings" "production" {
  project_id          = temps_project.web.id
  environment_id      = data.temps_environment.production.id
  max_concurrent_runs = 8
  retention_days      = 14
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (Number) ID of the environment.
- `project_id` (Number) ID of the project.

### Optional

- `drain_timeout_secs` (Number) Grace period for runs when a deployment stops.
- `host_service` (String) Service of the deployment that hosts the workflows.
- `inline_payload_limit_bytes` (Number) Largest payload kept in the journal itself.
- `invocation_deadline_secs` (Number) Longest a step may run.
- `lease_secs` (Number) How long a worker holds a run without reporting.
- `managed_store_service_id` (Number) Managed database that stores the journals.
- `max_active_runs` (Number) Runs started and not finished.
- `max_concurrent_runs` (Number) Runs executing at once.
- `max_journal_bytes_per_run` (Number) Journal size of one run.
- `max_payload_bytes` (Number) Largest input or output of a step.
- `max_steps_per_run` (Number) Steps one run may take.
- `retention_days` (Number) Days finished runs are kept.
- `stuck_after_failures` (Number) Failed attempts before a run is marked stuck.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Import ID, `<project_id>/<environment_id>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <project_id>/<environment_id>
terraform import temps_environment_workflow_settings.production 8/21
```
